relatedSnapshot.title: Fix campaign analytics uploaded leads denominator
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Issue

On the campaign Analytics tab, draft campaigns can show `0 / 1000 leads uploaded` in the Leads Contacted card even after leads have been uploaded. The denominator is currently derived from campaign analytics metadata/provider sync and falls back to `1000` when the metadata count is missing or zero.

 <image> 

 <image> 

## Expected behavior

The denominator should always reflect the true current number of leads uploaded to the campaign:

* Adding/importing leads should increase/update the denominator.
* Lead imports append/upsert and do not replace existing campaign leads.
* Deleting campaign leads should decrease/update the denominator.
* Draft campaigns should not depend on provider analytics sync to show the uploaded lead count.

## Proposed fix

Use the campaign lead relationship table count as the source of truth for the uploaded-leads denominator in the existing campaign metrics fetch, while keeping contacted/reply/positive/booked metrics sourced from analytics metadata/provider sync. Also invalidate the campaign detail metrics query after lead membership mutations so the UI refreshes immediately.

PR: Institute-of-Business-Growth/ai-clients#3639

relatedSnapshot.title: Campaigns launched with no leads get stuck in 'completed' status permanently
relatedSnapshot.description:
*Important to get this fixed quickly as campaigns are set to auto launch by default - if there is no leads by the time it's created they get stuck in this cycle. The only fix is to download the leads, delete the leads, and then duplicate the campaign and re-upload.*

## Bug Report

When an email campaign is launched with no leads uploaded yet, it transitions to **completed** status. Once leads are subsequently uploaded, the campaign remains stuck in **completed** and does not resume sending.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create and launch an email campaign with **no leads uploaded**
2. The campaign transitions to `completed` status (because Company One marks it as completed when there are no leads to send to)
3. Upload leads to the campaign
4. Campaign remains stuck in `completed` status — leads are never sent
5. User can manually resume the campaign → status changes to `active`
6. After 1-2 minutes, the campaign reverts back to `completed` again despite having leads

### Root Cause Analysis (Preliminary)

The issue appears to involve two interacting problems:

1. **Company One marks campaigns as completed (status 3) when launched with no leads.** This is expected Company One behavior — if there are no leads, the campaign has "nothing to do" so it completes immediately.
2. **Periodic sync overwrites local status with Company One's status.** The `syncCampaignData` Inngest function (`campaign-sync.ts`) and `campaign-import.ts` both call `mapInstantlyStatusToOur()` which maps Company One status `3` → `OutreachCampaignStatus.Completed`. This sync runs periodically and overwrites any local status changes.
3. **Resume only updates locally, not durably against sync.** When a user resumes, the app calls Company One's `/campaigns/{id}/activate` endpoint, which sets the campaign to active on Company One. However, if Company One transitions the campaign back to completed quickly (because it already processed and found no *new* unsent leads, or some race condition), the next sync cycle picks up `completed` again and overwrites the local `active` status.

### Key Files

* `lib/inngest/functions/campaign/util.ts` — `mapInstantlyStatusToOur()` (line 142)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/campaign-sync.ts` — status sync logic (line 304)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/campaign-import.ts` — import status mapping (line 323)
* `lib/inngest/functions/outreach/periodic-sync.ts` — periodic sync trigger
* `trpc/routers/outreach/campaigns.ts` — resume campaign endpoint (line 1889)

### Suggested Fix

The sync process should not overwrite a campaign's status to `completed` if the campaign has been resumed or has pending/unsent leads. Consider:

* Adding a guard in the sync that checks for uploaded leads before allowing transition to `completed`
* Preserving user-initiated status changes (e.g. resume) by skipping provider status sync for recently-resumed campaigns
* Not mapping Company One's `completed` status when the campaign has leads that haven't been contacted yet

relatedSnapshot.title: fix: optimize submission polling to prevent UI freeze after campaign creation
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Problem

After creating a campaign, the submission details page (`/dashboard/{workspace-slug}/submissions/{submissionId}`) freezes and becomes completely unresponsive, preventing users from navigating away or interacting with the UI. This affects the user experience for 15-20 minutes while campaigns are processing.

### Root Causes

1. **Excessive polling** - `ProcessingState` component polls every 2 seconds indefinitely
2. **No cleanup** - Polling continues even after component unmount or navigation
3. **Multiple queries** - `OutreachCreatorDisplay` adds another continuous query on top
4. **Background polling** - Polling continues even when tab is inactive

## Solution

Implemented multiple optimizations to fix the polling freeze:

### 1\. Optimized Polling Interval

* Changed from aggressive 2-second polling to 10 seconds initially
* Implemented exponential backoff: 10s → 15s → 30s → 60s (max)
* Reduces API calls by 80-95% while maintaining status updates

### 2\. Proper Cleanup Mechanisms

* Added `isMounted` ref to track component lifecycle
* Disabled React Query when component unmounts
* Removed polling in background tabs

### 3\. Visibility Detection

* Pause polling when tab is inactive using `document.visibilityState`
* Resume polling when user returns to tab
* Prevents unnecessary load when page isn't visible

### 4\. Conditional Query in OutreachCreatorDisplay

* Stop campaign query once submission is completed
* Only query while submission is still processing
* Eliminates redundant continuous queries

## Impact

✅ Dramatically reduced API call frequency (10-60s instead of 2s)  
✅ UI remains responsive during campaign processing  
✅ Users can navigate away without issues  
✅ Polling stops completely when component unmounts  
✅ No polling in inactive/background tabs

## Related PR

PR #831: <url:github.com>

## Files Modified

* `components/ai-tools/processing-state.tsx`
* `components/submissions/submission-displays/outreach-creator-display.tsx`

relatedSnapshot.title: Fix automation errors in AI-SDR cold email campaign
relatedSnapshot.description:
#### Customer Name

Name 16

#### Customer Email

<email>

#### Workspace name

Name 16

#### Screenshot

#### What are you trying to achieve?

Run a standard AI-SDR cold email campaign with automated meeting booking so prospects who reply can easily schedule calls using the connected calendar and Zoom meeting link.  The goal is for the AI to respond to replies and allow prospects to book one valid meeting within the allowed calendar window (9am–5pm CST).

#### What are you doing to achieve it?

The client launched an AI-SDR campaign inside Acquisity.  Steps taken:  • Configured AI campaign using the standard AI configuration template • Connected calendar for automated meeting booking • Set calendar rules to allow booking 9am–5pm CST only • Added Zoom meeting link inside AI configuration • Assigned the correct salesperson calendar (Name 17) • Campaign was turned on and began receiving replies  Campaign produced 14 positive replies within the first week.

#### What is happening instead?

Multiple automation and booking errors are occurring:  • AI sending multiple meeting invites to the same prospect • Prospects receiving duplicate booking links in the same thread • Prospects receiving multiple calendar invites across different days • AI referencing incorrect dates in emails • AI offering calendar times that are actually blocked • Calls being booked outside the allowed time window • Zoom link sometimes sending <domain> instead of the configured meeting link  Additional UI / workflow issues:  • If a prospect CCs another person, the CC contact does not appear in the Acquisity UI • One email thread is locked and cannot be opened or replied to • AI responded to a thread even though it was flagged for manual response  The client paused the campaign because these issues were causing confusion with prospects.

#### What is the expected outcome?

Expected behavior:  • AI should send one booking link only • Prospects should receive one meeting invite • Calendar should only offer available times within the allowed window • Meeting invite should include the correct Zoom link • If a thread is flagged for manual response, AI should not reply automatically • CC recipients should be visible in the Acquisity UI • Email threads should remain clickable and editable  Campaign should run normally without sending duplicate invites or incorrect scheduling information.
